facts.fact: UNICEF, the grant agent, reports that by June 2025 the digitisation of EMIS had been finalised and piloted, with no count of pilot schools given; deployment to 4,500 primary schools in 156 weredas, with 4,500 computers, was planned for July 2025 to June 2026 and had not begun.

The Ministry of Education developed and completed the web-based EMIS and finalised an EMIS Directive for it, with World Bank support; the system gives unique identification numbers to students, teachers and schools and covers federal, regional, woreda and school levels.

The platform was developed under a GPE System Capacity Grant through the World Bank, its school computers and training are paid from the GPE STEP grant through UNICEF, and US$15,062,600 of the grant's top-up is tied to EMIS digitisation; no domestic budget line is stated.

In the year to 29 June 2025 the real-time digitised EMIS was fully developed, tested and piloted, 1,322 EMIS and planning experts (132 women) were trained, and the tender for 4,500 primary-school computers was set for August 2025.
